name_reason: Name correctly encodes domain (dialog/shop), purpose (buy-for-whom confirm prompt), and datatype (text-id table). No Ghidra address residue; '_buy_for_' and the 6-element shop-tier dimension are domain semantics, not address suffixes. Matches data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention and its sibling tier tables in dlgtab.c.
purpose: Per-shop-tier FDTXT dialog page text-id for the 'buy for whom?' confirmation prompt in the chapter-intro shop buy menu.
logic_summary: Sole reader fd2_run_buy_item_menu block-copies the 12 bytes (3x MOVSD from 0x526FA @ 0x2F0CE) into a stack-local buffer at [ESP+0x2c], then on the confirm branch reads it back signed: MOVSX EAX, word ptr [ESP + cursor_state*2 + 0x48] @ 0x2F282, indexed by the shop-tier radio state data_fd2_chapter_intro_menu_cursor_state @ 0x5412B (0..5). The value is passed as the FDTXT page id to fd2_display_dialog_scene; fd2_text_dialog_typewriter_loop then reads the Yes/No reply (cursor_idx==1 means 'no'). This prompt precedes the party_total_gold<price affordability check.
element_semantics: Each element [tier] is the signed FDTXT dialog page id shown for the 'buy for whom?' confirm prompt at shop tier == data_fd2_chapter_intro_menu_cursor_state. Values {0x0001, 0x01F6, 0x0001, 0x01B7, 0x0001, 0x01B7}: tiers 0,2 use page 0x0001, tier 1 uses 0x01F6, tiers 3,5 use 0x01B7 (tier 4 also 0x0001).
comment_original_issue: The original src comment cited the readback instruction as 'MOVSX EAX, word ptr [ESP + cursor_state*2 + ...] @ 0x2F184'. Disassembly shows 0x2F184 is actually the no_equip table's readback (buffer [ESP+0x20] -> [ESP+EAX*2+0x3c]); the buy_for table (buffer [ESP+0x2c]) is read back at 0x2F282 -> [ESP+EAX*2+0x48]. Address corrected and the typewriter Yes/No follow-up noted.
notes: is_const=true confirmed: xrefs to 0x526FA are only DATA (0x2f0c9 MOV ESI) + READ (0x2f0ce MOVSD), no writers. Memory bytes 01 00 f6 01 01 00 b7 01 01 00 b7 01 match the src int16[6] initializer exactly. Ghidra plate was <null> (blank) before; created a concise plate mirroring the src conclusion. The 21 javac errors in run_script_inline output are pre-existing stale cached scripts in ghidra_scripts/, unrelated to this run (my script reported SCRIPT COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY).
